title: Signalsmith HQ_RENDER synthetic objective measurements
classification: objective regression/measurement only; synthetic fixtures do not establish sound-quality acceptance, listening quality, device performance, hardware behavior, or Roland fidelity

environment.runtime: Node.js invoking production TypeScript adapter and pinned Signalsmith Stretch WASM; no browser AudioWorklet or audio device used

methodology.input: deterministic synthetic signals, no random generator; 2.4 seconds/channel; harmonic mono pitch source at 220 Hz; four-partial decaying broadband transient; stereo phase-offset harmonic pair; vowel-like harmonic source at 110 Hz with Gaussian spectral bands centered at 650, 1200, and 2500 Hz

steadyWindow.sampleAlignment: input analysis window index is offset by result.leadingLatencySamples in rendered output

methodology.transient: 18 ms deterministic four-partial decaying burst beginning at 0.8 s; energy centroid measured within +/-120 ms; output centroid has result.leadingLatencySamples removed; peak ratio compares max absolute output/input samples in the ROI
methodology.stereo: zero-lag Pearson correlation over the same 1-second steady-state window in both channels, no lag search
methodology.formants: integrated FFT power in +/-18% nominal bands and pitch-shifted bands; reports relative band-energy movement, not formant-preservation quality
limitations: No listening panel or subjective quality rating
No hardware or real-time load benchmark
The offline render API does not expose an independent formant-preservation control

analysisWindow.peakEstimator: largest FFT power bin in +/-22% target range with parabolic interpolation of log power

stereoCoherence.note: Pearson correlation is measured without additional lag search over the aligned steady-state window; both channels are the same harmonic template with a fixed 0.92 rad phase offset.

source.type: deterministic harmonic synthesis with Gaussian amplitude bands

formantBandMovement.bandMethod: integrated Hann-window FFT power in +/-18% bands about each synthetic source center and the same center multiplied by the semitone ratio, compared before and after pitch shift

measurements.interpretation: Positive change means relatively more energy in the pitch-shifted band than the unshifted source band; it is not a formant-preservation score.
